gtcsolo.glossary.overclocking.title: Overclocking
gtcsolo.glossary.overclocking.text.1: Uses a higher voltage to perform the same operation faster. A normal overclock multiplies EU/t by four and halves the processing time for each step.
gtcsolo.glossary.overclocking.text.2: Throughput increases, but so does the total energy used per product. Overclocking is useful when power is plentiful or an operation is holding back production.
gtcsolo.glossary.overclocking.text.3: Available voltages and overclocking rules depend on the machine. Machines with perfect or industrial overclocking follow those rules instead.
gtcsolo.glossary.perfect_overclocking.te: Multiplies EU/t by four and reduces processing time to one quarter per step. This gives a larger speed increase while keeping the total energy per operation unchanged before rounding and time limits.
Requires a supported machine or conditions such as sufficient coil temperature. Behavior beyond the minimum processing time depends on support for sub-tick parallelization.
An overclock with a greater time reduction than the normal rule. For example, dividing duration by 2.25 per step provides more speed while retaining the usual fourfold increase in EU/t.
The duration factor and activation requirements belong to each machine. Check its introduction for conditions such as a registered sample or sufficient temperature.
gtcsolo.glossary.industrial_overclocking: Increases the material and product quantities handled per operation while gradually shortening processing time. The standard rule doubles input/output, quadruples EU/t and multiplies duration by 90% for each step.
Two steps give four times the input/output, sixteen times the EU/t and 81% of the original duration. Continuous material supply lets this production capacity perform at its best.
Machines with a separate base input/output bonus or parallel processing combine those factors as well. Check the machine introduction for its own adjustments, including temperature bonuses.
gtcsolo.glossary.io_bonus.title: Input/Output Bonus
gtcsolo.glossary.io_bonus.text.1: A multiplier on the materials and products handled in one operation. An eightfold input/output bonus consumes eight operations worth of materials and produces eight operations worth of output.
gtcsolo.glossary.io_bonus.text.2: The input/output bonus itself does not multiply EU/t. Power is determined separately by overclocking, parallel count and the machine rules. Supply and output handling must keep up with the increased quantities.
gtcsolo.glossary.io_bonus.text.3: A base bonus of eight combined with four parallels handles 32 operations worth of materials. Some machines fill bonus capacity only when additional materials arrive; follow their stated input locations and conditions.
gtcsolo.glossary.parallel.title: Parallel Processing
gtcsolo.glossary.parallel.text.1: Runs several copies of the same recipe at once. Normally, materials, products and EU/t scale with the parallel count while the duration of one operation stays the same.
gtcsolo.glossary.parallel.text.2: Reaching the configured limit requires enough materials, power and output space. Adding a Parallel Control Hatch cannot increase production beyond what the supply line supports.
gtcsolo.glossary.parallel.text.3: Some machines combine this with a separate input/output bonus or sub-tick parallelization. The machine introduction lists the supported mechanisms.
gtcsolo.glossary.subtick_parallel.title: Sub-tick Parallelization
gtcsolo.glossary.subtick_parallel.text.1: Converts overclocked processing time below one tick into additional operations handled together. There are normally 20 ticks per second.
gtcsolo.glossary.subtick_parallel.text.2: For example, an operation shortened to the equivalent of 0.25 ticks can process four copies in one tick. The inputs and outputs must support that larger batch.
gtcsolo.glossary.subtick_parallel.text.3: Only supported machines can use it. Whether it combines with ordinary parallel processing is also machine-specific.
gtcsolo.glossary.voltage_current.title: Voltage and Amperage
gtcsolo.glossary.voltage_current.text.1: Voltage describes the tier of a machine or recipe. Amperage is the number of packets of power carried at that voltage. Match machines, power supplies and cables to the required EU/t.
gtcsolo.glossary.voltage_current.text.2: Supported multiblocks can run recipes one voltage tier higher when they have multiple Energy Hatches at their highest supplied voltage. Two LV Energy Hatches let an Electric Blast Furnace run MV recipes.
gtcsolo.glossary.voltage_current.text.3: This changes the multiblock operating limit; it does not raise the voltage rating of cables or single-block machines. Choose wiring for both the voltage and amperage.
